claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A forward-deployed engineer is a customer-facing software engineer employed by a product company who helps implement that product inside a client company, often working alongside the client's employees for a defined period.
claims.quote: A **forward-deployed engineer** (**FDE**), also called a **forward-deployed software engineer** (**FDSE**), is a customer-facing [software engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_engineer "Software engineer") who works for a company that makes a product and helps implement that product within a client company, often working alongside the client's employees for a defined period of time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_deployed_engineer#cite_note-NewStack-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_deployed_engineer#cite_note-MarketWatchFDE-2)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The FDE role overlaps with solutions architects, sales engineers, customer engineers, professional services engineers, systems integrators, and IT consultants.
claims.quote: The responsibilities of forward-deployed engineers overlap with those of [solutions architects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solutions_architect "Solutions architect"), [sales engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sales_engineer "Sales engineer"), [customer engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customer_engineer "Customer engineer"), [professional services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_services "Professional services") engineers, [systems integrators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_integrator "Systems integrator"), and [information technology consultants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology_consulting "Information technology consulting").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_deployed_engineer#cite_note-NewStack-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_deployed_engineer#cite_note-MarketWatchFDE-2)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The term forward-deployed comes from U.S. military jargon.
claims.quote: The term "[forward-deployed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward-basing "Forward-basing")" comes from U.S. military jargon.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_deployed_engineer#cite_note-3)
